A.explanation: This is the symbol for an electric bell, shown by the dome shape. It produces sound from current, it does not act as a microphone.

B.explanation: This bowl-shaped symbol is a sounder or buzzer type output device. It does not represent a sound-to-signal input device.

C.explanation: This circle with a flat diaphragm bar on top is the microphone symbol. It converts incident sound waves into an electrical signal.

D.explanation: This flared horn shape is the symbol for a loudspeaker. It does the opposite of a microphone by converting electrical signal to sound.

hints: Look at the top part of each symbol - only one has a small flat bar above a circle to suggest a diaphragm picking up sound.
Recall the energy direction: a microphone changes sound wave energy into electrical energy, while a loudspeaker and bell change electrical energy into sound.
Compare the flared horn shape with the circle-and-bar shape to separate an output loudspeaker from an input microphone.
walkthrough: Identify what each diagram shows: A is a dome, B is an open bowl, C is a circle with a straight bar on top, D is a box with a wide flare on top.
State the function rule: a microphone is an input transducer that converts variations in sound pressure on a diaphragm into variations in current or voltage.
Recall the standard 9702 symbol: a small circle for the transducer body with a line above it for the diaphragm that receives the sound.
Match this to the diagrams: only C has the circle-plus-diaphragm form, while A is a bell and D is a loudspeaker output horn.
Conclude that the microphone description fits the circle-and-bar symbol. This is option C
